sources.title: Introduction to MADS-box genes
sources.fullVisibleTextRead: Introduction to MADS-box genes T he Arabidopsis genome contains a large family of MADS-box genes (approximately 30 to date have been cloned), and many of these play important roles in flower development. The MADS-box itself is a conserved region found at the 5' of all plant MADS-box genes. It encodes a DNA-binding domain found in other eukaryotic transcription factors, such as MCM1 from yeast, and SRF found in humans. The K-box is a region that codes for a protein domain that shows some similarity to the coiled coil structure of keratin. It is thought to be involved in protein-protein interactions. The MADS-box and K-box are separated by a weakly conserved Intervening ( I ) region, and a few MADS-box genes have an amino-terminal extension ( N ). The Carboxyl-terminal ( C ) region may function as a transcriptional activation domain. Selected References J. L. Riechmann and E. M. Meyerowitz, Biological Chemistry 378:1079-1101, 1997.
sources.conclusion: Generic Arabidopsis MADS-box family/domain description, no explicit Yanofsky-lab project, research question or implemented method. Gene cloning/DNA-binding/domain terms are field context, not lab-method evidence.
